re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. ## PR Description

Fixes #973

Shared composer `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart` — the app adapter (flutter_app) has no key code of its own, so both hosts get the fix.

## What was wrong
`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

## The fix (one branch in the existing Focus handler)
- Enter (main or numpad) **without Shift** → `_send(...)` + `KeyEventResult.handled` — never reaches the IME.
- **Shift+Enter** → falls through untouched, so the IME still inserts the break with any in-flight composing run (Cyrillic autocorrect) intact.
- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

Flutter routes key events to the platform/IME first or handler first? In Flutter, `Focus.onKeyEvent` handlers run BEFORE the event is given to the platform text input client? Actually Flutter's hardware keyboard events flow: key events from the platform → `HardwareKeyboard` → dispatch through focus tree (`FocusNode.onKeyEvent`). The text input plugin (IME) receives keys via the platform's own channel (on macOS, `NSView` interpretKeyEvents happens in the platform embedder before/parallel to sending key events to the framework?). On macOS the key event goes to `NSEvent` → FlutterView → the engine forwards to framework for dispatch; if the framework marks it handled, the engine doesn't pass to NSView's interpretKeyEvents (IME). If unhandled, the engine lets the IME/text input client process it. So plain Enter being handled means the IME never sees it — a composing run would NOT be committed by Enter; instead the composing text... hmm, the text is already in the field (composing region is just marked), so sending the text would send the composing text as-is, and the composing region might remain stale. ## PR Description

Fixes #973

Shared composer `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart` — the app adapter (flutter_app) has no key code of its own, so both hosts get the fix.

## What was wrong
`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

## The fix (one branch in the existing Focus handler)
- Enter (main or numpad) **without Shift** → `_send(...)` + `KeyEventResult.handled` — never reaches the IME.
- **Shift+Enter** → falls through untouched, so the IME still inserts the break with any in-flight composing run (Cyrillic autocorrect) intact.
- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

**Contract test** `packages/fa_ui/test/chat_composer_enter_test.dart` (macOS platform pinned — the owner's platform):

fails-pre (origin/main @ 13fc6abf):
```
00:00 +0: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline
Expected: true
  Actual: <false>
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline [E]
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter still sends
00:00 +1 -1: Some tests failed.
```
(`enterHandled` false pre-fix — plain Enter unhandled, nothing sent.)

passes-post (774731bc):
```
00:00 +2: All tests passed!
```

- `packages/fa_ui`: enter + ergonomics + surface_handlers + typing_footer → `+12: All tests passed!`

- `dart analyze` on changed files → no issues.

Note: `fa_chat_drop_test.dart` fails on pristine origin/main identically (verified via stash) — pre-existing, unrelated.

**No goldens**: key routing only — zero pixel/layout change (per issue workflow). No CI was dispatched.

`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

- Enter (main or numpad) **without Shift** → `_send(...)` + `KeyEventResult.handled` — never reaches the IME.
- **Shift+Enter** → falls through untouched, so the IME still inserts the break with any in-flight composing run (Cyrillic autocorrect) intact.
- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

```

Treating Shift as an unconditional "newline" modifier is defensible (it matches Discord/GitHub composers), but the PR description says *"Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send … unchanged"*, which is not true for the Shift+modifier combination. Either:

- document the decision in the doc comment above (one line: "Shift always means newline, even with Cmd/Ctrl"), or

## PR Description

Fixes #973

Shared composer `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart` — the app adapter (flutter_app) has no key code of its own, so both hosts get the fix.

## What was wrong
`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

Question: does intercepting plain Enter break an in-flight IME composing run on desktop (e.g., mid-Cyrillic composition)? With hardware keyboard composition (macOS accent menu, or IMEs), pressing Enter during composition usually commits the composition. Flutter routes key events to the platform/IME first or handler first? In Flutter, `Focus.onKeyEvent` handlers run BEFORE the event is given to the platform text input client? Actually Flutter's hardware keyboard events flow: key events from the platform → `HardwareKeyboard` → dispatch through focus tree (`FocusNode.onKeyEvent`). The text input plugin (IME) receives keys via the platform's own channel (on macOS, `NSView` interpretKeyEvents happens in the platform embedder before/parallel to sending key events to the framework?). On macOS the key event goes to `NSEvent` → FlutterView → the engine forwards to framework for dispatch; if the framework marks it handled, the engine doesn't pass to NSView's interpretKeyEvents (IME). If unhandled, the engine lets the IME/text input client process it. So plain Enter being handled means the IME never sees it — a composing run would NOT be committed by Enter; instead the composing text... hmm, the text is already in the field (composing region is just marked), so sending the text would send the composing text as-is, and the composing region might remain stale. The two tests cover the main path well (Shift+Enter unhandled + nothing sent + focus kept; plain Enter handled + sent + cleared; Cmd+Enter regression guard). Three cheap additions would pin the rest of the contract this branch introduces:

1. **Numpad Enter sends** — the new `LogicalKeyboardKey.numpadEnter` branch has no test at all:
   ```dart
   final numpadHandled = await tester.sendKeyEvent(LogicalKeyboardKey.numpadEnter);
   expect(numpadHandled, isTrue);
   expect(service.sentTexts, ['hello']);
   ```
2. **Ctrl+Enter sends** — only `metaLeft` is tested; the `isControlPressed` half of the condition (the default on Linux/Windows) is unverified. Same skeleton with `controlLeft`.
3. **Empty-field Enter no-ops** — `_send` guards `trimmed.isEmpty && _pendingAttachments.isEmpty`, but the handler still returns `handled`. Pin that Enter on an empty field sends nothing and stays handled (no stray newline) so a future refactor can't bypass the guard.

Optional 4th: a `KeyRepeatEvent` test (holding Enter must not multi-send) — the `event is! KeyDownEvent` early return covers it, but it's the kind of guard that silently regresses.

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 978
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/978
- **Title**: fix(#973): Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts newline in chat composer
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-973` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +111
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:00:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:00:54Z

## PR Description

Fixes #973

Shared composer `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart` — the app adapter (flutter_app) has no key code of its own, so both hosts get the fix.

## What was wrong
`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

## The fix (one branch in the existing Focus handler)
- Enter (main or numpad) **without Shift** → `_send(...)` + `KeyEventResult.handled` — never reaches the IME.
- **Shift+Enter** → falls through untouched, so the IME still inserts the break with any in-flight composing run (Cyrillic autocorrect) intact.
- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

## Evidence

**Contract test** `packages/fa_ui/test/chat_composer_enter_test.dart` (macOS platform pinned — the owner's platform):

fails-pre (origin/main @ 13fc6abf):
```
00:00 +0: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline
Expected: true
  Actual: <false>
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline [E]
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter still sends
00:00 +1 -1: Some tests failed.
```
(`enterHandled` false pre-fix — plain Enter unhandled, nothing sent.)

passes-post (774731bc):
```
00:00 +2: All tests passed!
```

**Scoped suites** (writable SDK copy, Flutter 3.47.5):
- `packages/fa_ui`: enter + ergonomics + surface_handlers + typing_footer → `+12: All tests passed!`
- `flutter_app` adapter `chat_composer_test.dart` (incl. Cmd+V smart paste) → `+13: All tests passed!`
- `dart analyze` on changed files → no issues.

Note: `fa_chat_drop_test.dart` fails on pristine origin/main identically (verified via stash) — pre-existing, unrelated.

**No goldens**: key routing only — zero pixel/layout change (per issue workflow). No CI was dispatched.

On macOS the key event goes to `NSEvent` → FlutterView → the engine forwards to framework for dispatch; if the framework marks it handled, the engine doesn't pass to NSView's interpretKeyEvents (IME). - **Title**: fix(#973): Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts newline in chat composer
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-973` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +111
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:00:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T12:00:54Z

## PR Description

Fixes #973

Shared composer `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart` — the app adapter (flutter_app) has no key code of its own, so both hosts get the fix.

## What was wrong
`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

## The fix (one branch in the existing Focus handler)
- Enter (main or numpad) **without Shift** → `_send(...)` + `KeyEventResult.handled` — never reaches the IME.
- **Shift+Enter** → falls through untouched, so the IME still inserts the break with any in-flight composing run (Cyrillic autocorrect) intact.
- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

## Evidence

**Contract test** `packages/fa_ui/test/chat_composer_enter_test.dart` (macOS platform pinned — the owner's platform):

fails-pre (origin/main @ 13fc6abf):
```
00:00 +0: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline
Expected: true
  Actual: <false>
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline [E]
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter still sends
00:00 +1 -1: Some tests failed.
```
(`enterHandled` false pre-fix — plain Enter unhandled, nothing sent.)

passes-post (774731bc):
```
00:00 +2: All tests passed!
```

**Scoped suites** (writable SDK copy, Flutter 3.47.5):
- `packages/fa_ui`: enter + ergonomics + surface_handlers + typing_footer → `+12: All tests passed!`
- `flutter_app` adapter `chat_composer_test.dart` (incl. Cmd+V smart paste) → `+13: All tests passed!`
- `dart analyze` on changed files → no issues.

Note: `fa_chat_drop_test.dart` fails on pristine origin/main identically (verified via stash) — pre-existing, unrelated.

**No goldens**: key routing only — zero pixel/layout change (per issue workflow). No CI was dispatched.

## PR Description

Fixes #973

Shared composer `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart` — the app adapter (flutter_app) has no key code of its own, so both hosts get the fix.

## What was wrong
`_handleComposerKey` only handled Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; bare Enter fell through to the IME, and with `TextInputAction.newline` the IME turned every desktop Enter into a line break. The owner had no Enter-to-send.

## The fix (one branch in the existing Focus handler)
- Enter (main or numpad) **without Shift** → `_send(...)` + `KeyEventResult.handled` — never reaches the IME.
- **Shift+Enter** → falls through untouched, so the IME still inserts the break with any in-flight composing run (Cyrillic autocorrect) intact.
- Touch keyboards: the return key arrives as an IME text delta under the kept `TextInputAction.newline` — no hardware key event, so mobile behavior (newline; send via button) is unchanged.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter send and Cmd/Ctrl+V smart paste: unchanged.

**Contract test** `packages/fa_ui/test/chat_composer_enter_test.dart` (macOS platform pinned — the owner's platform):

fails-pre (origin/main @ 13fc6abf):

  Actual: <false>
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: plain Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline [E]
00:00 +0 -1: desktop: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter still sends
00:00 +1 -1: Some tests failed.
```
(`enterHandled` false pre-fix — plain Enter unhandled, nothing sent.)

passes-post (774731bc):
```
00:00 +2: All tests passed!
```

- `packages/fa_ui`: enter + ergonomics + surface_handlers + typing_footer → `+12: All tests passed!`
- `flutter_app` adapter `chat_composer_test.dart` (incl. Cmd+V smart paste) → `+13: All tests passed!`
- `dart analyze` on changed files → no issues.

Note: `fa_chat_drop_test.dart` fails on pristine origin/main identically (verified via stash) — pre-existing, unrelated.

**No goldens**: key routing only — zero pixel/layout change (per issue workflow). No CI was dispatched.
